nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.rationale: Kalshi's KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS rules give only the team name and event date (rules_secondary is empty), so the format comes from the official NBA 2026 Kia Shooting Stars rules PDF (read directly 2026-11-09, sha256 ed035e65...b921; completeness/source_provenance/NBA_2026_Shooting_Stars.json): four teams of three (two NBA players plus one NBA Legend); seven locations shot in order 1 to 7 worth 2, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 4 points (right-lane layup/dunk, 18-ft right baseline, right elbow, right-wing three, top of the key, left-corner three, long-range three); each player takes one shot at each of locations 1-6 in the team's declared shooting order and at location 7 players shoot in that order as many times as the clock allows; a designated passer at the left wing feeds each shot; the team advances as a unit; 1:10 clock per team per round; the top two of four teams advance from round 1; the lower round-1 team shoots first in the final and the higher final-round score wins; a tied round-1 result that decides advancement is rerun among the tied teams only at 30 seconds (round-1 scores ignored); a tied final is rerun for the full 1:10; a shot out of the declared player order does not count (and, other than at location 7, that player does not shoot again); a team is disqualified if not all players make valid attempts from a location or if it shoots from locations out of order. What stays unknown: how Kalshi applies those rules to settlement and, from the PDF itself, what counts as a valid shot attempt, what disqualification does to a team's score or advancement, whether the 30-second tiebreaker still runs locations 1-6 in full, and whether the two players must be current NBA players. Four of the seven locations (right-lane layup/dunk, 18-ft right baseline, right elbow, top of the key) are 2-point spots, so make rates there come from nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill and only the right-wing three, left-corner three and long-range three come from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile. A Legend is likely to have little or no current shooting data, so team skill mixes current rates for active players with older evidence; tempo matters as in the 3PT contest.
nba.shooting_stars_team_skill.measurement: FORMAT (verified from the official NBA rules PDF, sha256 ed035e65...b921): 4 teams x 3 players (2 NBA players + 1 NBA Legend); locations 1-7 in order = right-lane layup/dunk 2, 18-ft right baseline 2, right elbow 2, right-wing three 3, top of the key 2, left-corner three 3, long-range three 4; at locations 1-6 each player takes one shot in the team's declared order, at location 7 players shoot in that order as many times as the clock allows; a left-wing passer feeds each shot; the team advances as a unit; clock = 1:10 per team per round; round 1 = all four teams, top two advance; the lower round-1 team shoots first in the final; the higher final-round score wins (that round-1 scores do not otherwise carry is an inference from this wording, the PDF ignores them explicitly only in the first-round tiebreaker); first-round tiebreaker = tied teams rerun at 30 seconds, only that score counts; final tiebreaker = rerun for the full 1:10; a shot out of the declared player order does not count (and outside location 7 that player does not shoot again); a team is disqualified if not all players make valid attempts from a location or if it shoots from locations out of order. SCORE = 2*(correct-order makes at locations 1, 2, 3, 5) + 3*(makes at locations 4, 6) + 4*(makes at location 7). STILL UNKNOWN (PDF silent; carried as explicit labelled assumptions, never as facts): (U1) what a valid shot attempt is; (U2) what disqualification does to a team's score or advancement; (U3) whether the 30-second tiebreaker still runs locations 1-6 in full or only location 7; (U4) how many location-7 attempts each player completes inside 1:10 and whether the clock can run out before location 7 (EMPIRICAL_QUESTION); (U5) whether other editions use the same rules; (U6) Kalshi's treatment of ties, disqualification, replay and cancellation (u10b). Estimation: NBA players' P(make) at the right-wing three, left-corner three and long-range three from nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile and at the 2-point locations from nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill; legend component: last five career seasons' 3P% and FT% with an age discount of 1.5 points of 3P% per year since retirement, shrunk to past legends' contest make rate with k = 50 shots, plus a shot-tempo term for the legend's attempts inside the clock; simulate 20,000 contests under the verified rules including the round-1 selection of two of four, with the tiebreak rules and a disqualification and out-of-order branch as labelled assumptions (size of the branch is empirical, not stated by the PDF), and report P(win). CONTRACT CONSTRAINT: KXNBASHOOTINGSTARS settles on which named team wins the contest; the 30-second rerun matters when a tie needs to be broken to decide the two final teams (for example a tie for the second slot or a multi-team tie across the cut), the full 1:10 rerun only if the final ends level, and Kalshi's text has no tie, shoot-off, disqualification or team-change clause, so how Kalshi settles a tie, disqualification or replay is unknown (its terms could not be read here); the league's rules PDF gives only the league's own tiebreakers.

nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill.measurement: Per player and per 2-point location type. Rim location: P(make) from uncontested restricted-area finishing (dunk and layup action types) over the last 3 seasons, shrunk to the position-group rate with k = 60 attempts (placeholder); the main output there is seconds per attempt. Baseline, elbow and top of key: mid-range FG% by zone (left/right baseline, elbow, free-throw-line extended) over 3 seasons from shot-level rows, shrunk to the player's overall mid-range rate with k = 80 attempts (placeholder); a catch-and-shoot restriction by zone is UNVERIFIED and UNAVAILABLE from any free source shown here, so until one is found the rate is an all-attempt mid-range rate flagged as contested-biased, blended with career FT% at weight 0.3 (placeholder) when attempts are below 40. Legends: last five career seasons' mid-range FG% and FT% with an age discount of 2 points of mid-range FG% per year since retirement (placeholder), shrunk to the legend pool with k = 50 shots; rim finishing for a legend is an imputed rate with a flagged ceiling. Tempo: seconds from pass to release per location type (hand-coded). The official 2026 rules PDF fixes the point values (2 at locations 1, 2, 3 and 5), the one-shot-per-player rule at locations 1-6 and the declared shooting order; which player shoots which location is the team's pre-declared order (one shot each at locations 1-6, so each of the three players shoots every 2-point location once). Output per-player P(make) and seconds per attempt for the four 2-point location types; as-of = team and shooting-order announcement.

nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill.mechanism: Four of the seven Shooting Stars locations (right-lane layup/dunk, 18-ft right baseline, right elbow, top of the key) are 2-point locations (official 2026 rules PDF) whose make rates depend on rim finishing and catch-and-shoot mid-range skill and on how fast the shooter receives the pass and releases; they are not predicted by three-point spot accuracy.
nba.shooting_stars_two_point_spot_skill.rationale: nba.threept_spot_and_tempo_profile is built from three-point locations and the 27+ ft rate, so with four of seven locations worth two points it leaves most of the circuit without a skill estimate. Layup/dunk locations are expected (an assumption to be estimated, no source) to be high-percentage for athletes, so the differentiator there is time per attempt and, for a legend, whether he can still finish at the rim; baseline, elbow and top-of-key are mid-range catch-and-shoot shots where current players have season data and legends do not. The location list and point values are taken from the official 2026 rules PDF (read directly 2026-11-09, sha256 ed035e65...b921).
